comparison: Both evaluate claims C1-C2 regarding lnc-FANCI-2 upregulation in cervical lesion progression and regulation by E7/YY1. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes citation to prior work (Liu et al., 2021), while peer reviewers explicitly list these as key strengths of the study.

Both address phenotypic changes in knockout cells (C73-C78, C81). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by morphological and functional assays with dose-dependent effects. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'convincing evidence' without specific challenges, also noting C80 (senescence data).

Both evaluate pathway-level findings from RNA-seq (C105-C111). OpenEval finds GSEA analysis SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical thresholds. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly lists increased RAS signaling and decreased IFN pathways as a strength, fully accepting these conclusions.

Both address molecular changes including phosphorylated Akt/Erk and protein expression changes (C3-C10, overlapping with C8-C10, C116, C121-C123). OpenEval finds comprehensive characterization SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly lists these molecular findings as strengths, accepting the evidence.

Both evaluate proteomic profiling results (C82-C88, C90). OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED with reasonable cutoffs, noting 60% RNA-protein concordance. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data as a strength, though there appears to be a directional discrepancy in the reviewer's summary of MCAM regulation.

Both address RNA-protein interaction findings (C11, C158) identifying MAP4K4 as a binding partner. OpenEval finds IRPCRP-mass spectrometry data SUPPORTED with appropriate validation. Peer reviewers accept protein-protein interaction analyses as part of convincing evidence without specific challenges.

Both evaluate MAP4K4 functional data (C12, C162-C163). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED that MAP4K4 knockdown increases p-Akt/p-Erk similar to lnc-FANCI-2 loss. Peer reviewers do not challenge these mechanistic findings, accepting them as part of the RAS pathway regulation evidence.

Both address clinical correlations from TCGA data (C13, C51, C148-C149, C210-C211). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant survival analysis and expression correlations. Peer reviewers accept that the study provides 'convincing evidence that lnc-FANCI-2 affects cervical cancer outcome' without challenging clinical data.

Both evaluate the main mechanistic conclusions (C14, C49-C51, C117-C118, C126, C138, C165, C213-C214). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED but notes 'intrinsically' may be overstated. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the study provides 'convincing evidence' for RAS pathway regulation and 'important new insights,' representing full acceptance of central conclusions.

Both address expression patterns of lnc-FANCI-2 across cell lines (C52-C63, overlapping C55-C63). OpenEval finds data SUPPORTED by multiple methods but notes HPV18+ absence is unexplained. Peer reviewers accept these descriptive findings as part of foundational characterization without challenge.
